title: Rewrite Sanity & Regression Playbook — code generation + refactoring
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight playbook for onboarding/refinement/regression checks focused on code generation and automated refactoring prompts. The goal: detect regressions that break compilation, unit test behavior, or introduce style/complexity regressions when we onboard new model revisions or change prompt families.

Scope and intent:
- Languages: primary focus on Python (3.9+), secondary coverage for Go and Java methods where easy compilation checks exist.
- Types of prompts: generation-from-spec, automated-refactor (extract function, rename variable, reduce nesting), add-tests (generate unit tests), and formatting/style transformations.
- Not exhaustive e2e correctness; intended as a fast, repeatable gate for model rollout stages (canary -> gradual -> wide).

Test matrix (quick reference):
1) Compilation/Import sanity (fast):
   - For Python: ensure generated files import without exception (pyflakes/AST import check + run import in isolated process).
   - For Java/Go: attempt compile (javac/go build) in container.
   - Failure mode: syntax error, missing imports, incompatible language features.

2) Unit test pass (gold):
   - Run existing unit tests (seeded small harness) against generated code if tests are part of prompt scenario.
   - Triage: test failures should be classified as behavioral regressions vs. brittle test expectations.

3) Style & linting (signal):
   - Run flake8/ruff (Python) or golangci-lint for Go. Track new violations introduced by model output vs. baseline.
   - Track auto-format diff size (black/clang-format). Large diffs = suspicious refactor.

4) Complexity/regression delta (heuristic):
   - Compute basic metrics: LOC, cyclomatic complexity, function length, nesting depth.
   - Flag >20% increase in complexity or >30% LOC growth for the same task.

5) Semantic equivalence / behavioral heuristics (soft):
   - For refactor prompts that must preserve semantics, run property checks where possible (smoke inputs, golden outputs, randomized fuzz).
   - Use lightweight metamorphic tests for ML-generated code (e.g., idempotence checks).

Prompt families and sample prompts:
- extract_small_function: "Refactor the block in process_data into a separate helper named parse_rows without changing external behavior. Preserve docstring. Show the new file content."
- simplify_conditionals: "Rewrite this if/elif chain as clearer early returns or guard clauses, keep same semantics and tests passing."
- add_unit_tests: "Write 6 pytest unit tests for validate_input covering edge cases and error branches. Use parametrize where helpful."
- preserve_api_contract: "Refactor internals but keep function signatures and public behavior stable. Do not change return types or raise new exception classes."

Each prompt family should be paired with one or more canonical scenarios:
- Tiny widget parser (200 lines): compile + 12 unit tests (fast)
- Config merging util (50 lines): complexity-sensitive, style-focused
- Numeric algorithm (FIR filter stub, deterministic): semantic-preservation harness with random seeds

Evaluation harness (implementation notes):
- Runner: containerized job performing steps: format-check -> compile/import -> lint -> run unit tests -> metric collection -> artifact snapshot (model prompt, model output, diffs).
- Runtime budget: 90s per sample for hosted CI gate (reduce sample count if time exceeds).
- Sampling: for models with stochastic outputs, collect N=3 outputs per prompt and apply majority/any-fail policies depending on metric.

Scoring and thresholds (suggested defaults):
- Hard fail: compilation/import error for any of the N outputs in canary policy; unit test regression where baseline passes and new output fails.
- Soft fail/warn: >10 new linter violations vs. baseline; average cyclomatic delta >20%; autoformat diff >35% of file lines.
- Alert level mapping:
   - FAIL-GRAVITY: block rollout, require patch or prompt rollback
   - WARN: allow limited canary but require monitoring and exception documented

Baseline and drift tracking:
- For each prompt id, store baseline artifacts: canonical prompt text, seed model version, sample outputs (N=5), baseline metrics (compiles?, tests_passed, lints, complexity).
- On each new model run, compute delta vector and persist. Use historical window (30 days) to compute mean/stdev and detect outliers.

Rubric for triage (example):
- If compilation errors appear: capture trace, diff vs baseline AST, label as 'syntax/regression', route to applied-ml+serving-runtime for kernel/encoding investigation (common cause: tokenizer truncation, newlines/escape sequences).
- If tests fail but compiles: run with debug prints, compare stack traces to baseline failing tests, check for nondeterministic seeds.
- If style regressions: determine if caused by model switching to a different idiom (e.g., f-strings vs % formatting). If acceptable, update baseline after approval.

Operational playbook for a failing canary:
1) Freeze rollout.
2) Capture artifact bundle and post to ticket (include prompt, model version, seed, raw output, test artifacts, lint diffs).
3) Re-run with deterministic settings (temperature=0, top_p=1) to check for sampling noise.
4) If deterministic fails -> block. If only stochastic fails -> consider stricter policy (require N=3 deterministic success).
5) If acceptable but borderline (WARN), tag experiment and monitor metrics on production traffic for 24h.

Examples (short):
- Prompt: "Refactor function compute_total to extract duplicate tax calculation into _compute_tax helper and keep behavior identical."
  - Baseline: compiles, 8 tests pass, flake8=0, complexity=4
  - New model: compiles, tests=7/8 (one failing decimal edge case) -> classify behavioral regression, block until reproducer and fix.

- Prompt: "Generate unit tests for normalize_input covering spaces and punctuation."
  - Baseline: N/A (new prompt), seed model version used to create baseline tests.
  - New model: tests generated but use deprecated assertRaises usage and stylistically inconsistent; lint diff small, accept and normalize in baseline after review.

Data collected per run (minimum):
- prompt_id, prompt_text
- model_version, deterministic_flags (temp, top_p, seed)
- raw_output (trimmed), artifact file(s) produced
- compile_result: ok|syntax_error|import_error
- unit_test_result: pass_count/fail_count and failing trace snippets
- lint_summary: total_violations and top rule ids
- complexity_metrics: LOC, max_fn_len, avg_cyclomatic
- diff_to_baseline: formatted unified diff size (lines changed)

UX + integration notes:
- Console should show quick green/red tiles for compile/test/lint with expandable artifact view and diffs.
- Allow engineer to mark a regression as false-positive and promote current output to new baseline with justification note (audit trail required).

Known limitations / caveats:
- Some transformations (large refactors) legitimately change LOC and style; heuristics can be noisy. Human review necessary for borderline cases.
- Unit tests generated by models are brittle; prefer seeded gold tests when possible.
- Language features: newer syntax (pattern matching, etc.) may fail on older runners; ensure CI runners match target runtime.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: How to best handle multi-file refactors where helper moved to different module? Current harness only snapshots per-file. TODO: extend snapshot to module-level refactor detection.
- Q: Do we accept behavioural changes that fix flaky tests but change semantics? Policy decision needed.
- TODO: add Go and Java canonical scenarios and quick compile templates.
- TODO: add AST-level semantic diffing prototype (use tree-sitter or lib2to3 AST comparison) to reduce false-positive behavioral flags.

Appendix: quick checklist for prompt onboarding run (copyable):
- [ ] Create canonical prompt + short description + expected invariants
- [ ] Add baseline artifacts (model version, sample outputs)
- [ ] Add unit test harness or golden inputs if available
- [ ] Run CI harness with new model revision (N=3)
- [ ] Review compile/test/lint tiles, attach triage notes if failing
- [ ] Decide: promote baseline / file bug / block rollout

Notes to self: keep this doc minimal and iterate. We should ship a small tutorial notebook demonstrating the harness end-to-end (python) to help partner teams run locally.

---
Last quick references:
- Example job pipeline: gh action -> docker image python:3.11 -> run flake8/black -> pytest -q -> store artifacts in S3 (prefix prompt_id/model_ver/date)
- Triage tags: regression:compilation, regression:unit-test, regression:style, regression:complexity

Contact: Anya (owner) for process questions; Mateo for CI infra; Jenna for prompt design.
